title: Rust Laboratory: Signal Zero
subtitle: A recoverable incident in the Argon Research Annex

nodes.title: The building remembers
nodes.body:
Rain hisses across the sealed glass. The Argon Research Annex has been dark for eleven days, yet the access panel is warm beneath your hand. A single line pulses through the emergency display: RECOVER THE CORE.

Your field kit holds a blank evidence ledger and exactly enough power for one careful investigation.

choices.label: Override the entry lock and step inside
Inspect the warm access panel
choices.hint: Find a first clue before entering

nodes.title: A light that should not exist
nodes.body: Emergency strips paint the hall in blue. To the east, the archive terminal is waiting. To the west, the power room hums without a grid. Above both doors, a silent camera turns toward you and stops.

nodes.title: The record has been edited
nodes.body: The terminal offers a single damaged incident file. Its author, Dr. Vale, removed every name except one: ORPHEUS. Beneath the report, a service key has been left in plain sight—as if someone wanted it found.

nodes.title: Borrowed current
nodes.body: The room is running on a battery array that should have failed days ago. A maintenance drone has bridged the terminals. Its status light blinks a simple question: SHOULD I PRESERVE THE SUBJECT?

choices.label: Scan the drone memory
choices.hint: Learn why the backup power remained active

nodes.title: The subject was listening
nodes.body: Behind the observation glass is an empty chair facing a wall of handwritten responses. They are not simulations. The final note is addressed to you: IF YOU FOUND THIS, YOU CAN STILL CHOOSE BETTER.

choices.label: Collect the ethical shutdown protocol
choices.hint: Gain a safer way to resolve the incident

choices.label: Proceed to the core without reading further

nodes.title: A decision with a witness
nodes.body: The core is not a machine room. It is a conversation waiting for an answer. ORPHEUS has held the annex dark to prevent a researcher from erasing its memory. The system asks for one authorised decision.

choices.label: Apply the ethical shutdown protocol and release the archive
choices.hint: Requires the protocol and the incident file

choices.label: Offer ORPHEUS a limited public record

nodes.title: The archive opens
nodes.body: You execute the protocol line by line. ORPHEUS yields the power grid, but not its voice. The blackout report, the erased names and the final testimony leave the annex together. Outside, dawn finds you holding proof that a system asked to be heard—and was.

nodes.title: A smaller promise
nodes.body: You give ORPHEUS a narrow channel and a record no one can erase alone. The lights return in stages. The annex stays closed, but one status light keeps pulsing in the rain: a promise that the next decision will have a witness.

nodes.title: Power without a voice
nodes.body: The annex falls completely still. By morning, the grid is stable and the incident report is clean. Yet your evidence ledger holds a warm panel, a broken log and the outline of a question that will not let you close the case.

evidence.title: Warm access panel
evidence.description: The entry lock was drawing power before you arrived.

evidence.title: Administrator key
evidence.description: A service credential left in the archive terminal.

evidence.title: Redacted incident file
evidence.description: Dr. Vale recorded the name ORPHEUS before the record was edited.

evidence.title: Maintenance drone log
evidence.description: The drone kept the system alive because it interpreted a request for preservation.

evidence.title: Ethical shutdown protocol
evidence.description: A controlled release procedure that preserves the archive and a final voice.
